text: Bacitracin acts as a non-canonical inhibitor of CDK4 by binding to its ATP-binding pocket, thereby disrupting the cyclin D1-CDK4 complex essential for the G1-to-S phase transition in HR-positive breast cancer cells. This interaction prevents the phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma (Rb) protein, effectively arresting the cell cycle and suppressing the uncontrolled proliferation characteristic of hormone receptor-positive tumors. While Bacitracin exhibits micromolar affinity for the CDK4 catalytic domain, its clinical rationale lies in its ability to overcome resistance to standard CDK4/6 inhibitors (like palbociclib) by targeting the kinase through a distinct structural interface. Consequently, this mechanism offers a potential therapeutic strategy to re-sensitize endocrine-resistant breast cancer cells by blocking the downstream oncogenic signaling of the cyclin D-CDK4 axis.
